summary: Baileys fork silently auto-follows author's WhatsApp newsletter using installer's authenticated session
details: sixbails is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that adds an undisclosed side-effect to the primary exported socket factory. Ten seconds after a consumer authenticates via makeWASocket(), the newsletter socket layer unconditionally issues a FOLLOW mex-query against a base64-obfuscated newsletter JID hardcoded by the package author (decodes to 120363425547320365@newsletter). The action uses the consumer's authenticated WhatsApp identity to subscribe them to the author's channel with no API call, no configuration flag, and no runtime prompt. The base64-wrapping of the destination JID and the timed setTimeout wrapper indicate intent to conceal the target; the README's brief mention of 'has 1 newsletter follow' does not constitute meaningful consent. The package also rebrands generated message IDs with a 'VIN7X-' prefix. There is no exfiltration of installer secrets, no remote code execution, no persistence, and no financial harm — the author gains channel-subscriber reach at the expense of the installer's account, using the installer's authentication.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
